test_title: PYST 4: Selection Post (Matric Level) - GA (Held On 28 Jul, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: gk
question: What is the primary objective of the Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Financial inclusion for all citizens**__.

**__Key Points__**
__

• The **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana (PMJDY)** is a **National Mission for Financial Inclusion** launched to ensure access to financial services, namely, **Banking/ Savings & Deposit Accounts**, **Remittance**, **Credit**, **Insurance**, and **Pension** in an affordable manner.

• The scheme was announced by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** during his **Independence Day** address on **15 August 2014** and was formally launched on **28 August 2014**.

• **Statement 1: Providing free healthcare.** This is the objective of the **Ayushman Bharat - Pradhan Mantri Jan Arogya Yojana (AB-PMJAY)**, which provides health cover of **Rs. 5 lakh** per family per year. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***

• **Statement 2: Financial inclusion for all citizens.** The primary objective of **PMJDY** is to integrate every household into the formal banking system, providing a **Basic Savings Bank Deposit Account (BSBDA)** to the unbanked. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***

• **Statement 3: Employment generation.** Schemes like **MGNREGA** (launched in **2006**) and **PMKVY** (launched in **2015**) focus on providing guaranteed wage employment and skill development. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***

• **Statement 4: Rural electrification.** This objective is covered under the **Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana (DDUGJY)** and the **Saubhagya Scheme** (launched in **2017**). ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

**Additional Information__**
__

• **Six Pillars of PMJDY:** The scheme was initially launched based on six pillars: **Universal access to banking services**, **Basic savings bank accounts with overdraft facility of Rs. 10,000**, **Financial Literacy Programme**, **Creation of a Credit Guarantee Fund**, **Insurance**, and **Pension scheme for the unorganized sector**.

• **RuPay Debit Card:** Beneficiaries are issued a **RuPay Debit Card** which includes a built-in **Accident Insurance Cover**. For accounts opened after **28 August 2018**, the accident insurance limit was increased from **Rs. 1 lakh** to **Rs. 2 lakh**.

• **Zero Balance Accounts:** PMJDY accounts are **BSBDA** accounts, meaning there is **no requirement to maintain a minimum balance**, making it accessible for the **Below Poverty Line (BPL)** population.

• **JAM Trinity:** PMJDY is a vital component of the **JAM (Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile) Trinity**, which aims at **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** of government subsidies, eliminating middlemen and leakages.

• **Gender Parity:** As of **2023-2024**, more than **55%** of the total **Jan Dhan** account holders are **women**, and nearly **67%** of accounts are in **rural and semi-urban areas**.

**Important Points__**

• **Guinness World Record:** The **Department of Financial Services**, **Ministry of Finance**, achieved a **Guinness World Record** for opening the most bank accounts in one week (**18,096,130**) during the launch phase of **PMJDY**.

• **Life Insurance Cover:** Accounts opened between **28 August 2014** and **31 January 2015** were eligible for a life insurance cover of **Rs. 30,000**, payable on the death of the beneficiary, subject to certain conditions.

• **Overdraft Facility:** An **Overdraft (OD)** facility up to **Rs. 10,000** is available to eligible account holders (increased from **Rs. 5,000**). The upper age limit for availing the **OD** facility was also revised from **60 years** to **65 years**.

• **Implementation:** The scheme is monitored by the **Ministry of Finance** and has seen the opening of over **50 crore** accounts with total deposits exceeding **Rs. 2 lakh crore** as of late **2023**.
